text:
The court will most likely grant the motion to remand. Under 28 U.S.C. §1441(a), only a defendant can remove a case, so a plaintiff who chose state court has no removal right, even though the federal claims could have been filed in federal court originally. This conflicts with the team note's "retain" options, which I don't think are legally right: timely removal and federal claims don't cure a plaintiff's lack of removal authority, and the judge's hostility toward the attorney isn't a basis for retaining the case.

CONFIDENCE: 90
